label: leadership development and partner management
overview: Leadership development in a professional services firm operates across two distinct dimensions: developing the next generation of leaders through a structured promotion pathway, and managing the conduct and culture of the existing leadership group. The most common failure in CA and advisory firm leadership is promoting technically excellent practitioners into leadership roles without assessing their leadership capability — creating leaders who are brilliant at the work but ineffective at developing people, managing conduct, and making partnership-level decisions. A rigorous promotion checklist, a conduct management framework, and the use of personality profiling tools (particularly the Enneagram) together provide a comprehensive approach to building and sustaining a high-quality leadership culture.

diagnostic_entry.primary_question: Is the leadership challenge primarily about developing and promoting the next generation of leaders, managing conduct or performance issues within the existing leadership group, building self-awareness and communication effectiveness across the team, or maintaining ethical standards and accountability?
diagnostic_entry.leadership_pipeline: When the firm's leadership pipeline is thin — when there are no credible internal succession candidates for partner or management roles — the intervention requires a structured development pathway, not just a promotion checklist. The checklist defines the destination; the development pathway defines how candidates get there.
diagnostic_entry.conduct_management: When an existing leader is behaving in ways that are inconsistent with the firm's values or performance expectations, a structured conduct management process is required. The process must be evidence-based, consistently applied, and separated from personality conflicts — which are the most common source of conduct management failures.
diagnostic_entry.self_awareness_and_communication: When leadership effectiveness is being undermined by interpersonal friction, communication breakdowns, or leadership style mismatches, personality profiling provides the shared language and framework for productive conversations. The Enneagram is particularly effective in professional services contexts because it addresses motivational drivers, not just behavioural patterns.
diagnostic_entry.ethical_standards: When conduct issues involve professional ethics, the intervention must be both developmental and consequential. A demerit system provides a graduated, transparent, and consistent accountability mechanism that treats ethics breaches seriously without defaulting immediately to dismissal for first-time or minor infractions.

materials.name: Directorship Pathway Guidelines
materials.summary: A transparent five-year roadmap into partnership, with strict benchmarks for experience, character and competency so promotion stops being a judgement call. It protects the firm as much as it develops the candidate: proven track record, cultural alignment, and personal financial affairs in order. Pathway 2 carries the competency assessment itself, rated 1 to 5 from "needs serious attention" to "competent to coach others effectively".
materials.who_when: Professional service firms, accounting practices and mid-sized businesses cultivating internal talent for equity partnership or directorship.
steps: Identify the Partner in Pathway and allocate them an Assessment Partner to own the relationship.
Introduce them to the Directorship Pathway 1 guidelines so the five-year timeline, the expected CPD hours and the requirement to submit at least two formal white papers are understood from the start.
Check the baseline before investing in competency testing — around 30 months of firm experience, $250k of fees managed, and $125k of organic fee growth generated.
Confirm the character guidelines are met: culturally aligned, insurable, a family trust in place, and personal financial affairs in good order.
Run the competency assessment from the Directorship Pathway 2 grid as a 360-degree review across Get Organised, Get the Job and Do the Job.
Have the candidate rate themselves 1 to 5 on competencies such as securing profitable engagements, chairing a formal directors' meeting, delegation, debt recovery and financial management.
Compare their self-rating against the average of the existing partners, and treat the gaps as the coaching plan rather than a verdict.
At the end of the five-year maximum, either move them into sharing equity and risk, or exit them as terminally unsuitable — the pathway does not run indefinitely.

materials.name: Enneagram-Based Employment Questions
materials.summary: Takes interviewing past technical competence to the motivations, stress triggers and social preferences underneath, using the nine Enneagram types and the broader work styles they group into — Soloists, Initiators and Cooperators. It lets an owner build a balanced team and anticipate how someone behaves under pressure, and it gives the interviewer questions sharp enough to reveal genuine self-awareness.
materials.who_when: Hiring managers, executive coaches and advisors doing advanced vetting for leadership, management or highly collaborative roles.
steps: Use it during the associate phase, before any partnership decision is on the table.
Identify the candidate's core type from the nine — Reformer, Achiever, Peacemaker, Investigator, Challenger, Enthusiast and the rest.
Ask the question built for that type rather than a generic one — an Investigator how they cope when they know others are wrong; a Challenger how they hold back sarcasm in the face of incompetence.
Probe an Achiever on how they cope when those around them appear to be having more success, and an Enthusiast on how they organise themselves across competing tasks.
Evaluate how they handle conflict, how they prioritise under pressure, and how they behave inside a team.
Read the answers for self-awareness and emotional intelligence — that is the signal the exercise exists to produce, not the type label itself.
Use the profile afterwards to align the role to natural strengths and to anticipate the friction points before they appear.

materials.name: Partner Accountability & Conduct Framework
materials.summary: The governance layer: a Code of Conduct, a Conduct & Effect matrix, and a points system that ties behaviour directly to money. Demerits accumulate against profit share — 20 points inside 12 months triggers immediate resignation and forfeiture of the client base — while a bonus system rewards growth. It also names boardroom manipulation tactics so toxic behaviour can be labelled objectively instead of argued about emotionally.
materials.who_when: Existing boards, established partnerships and executive teams needing strict governance, conflict resolution or formal performance management.
steps: On acceptance as a partner, integrate them into the framework immediately and have them sign the Code of Conduct.
Make sure they understand the difference between Gross Negligence and a Mistake, and how demerit and bonus points reach their profit share.
Assess partners regularly against the Finder, Minder, Grinder matrix — securing new clients, maintaining existing relationships, and delivering the technical work.
Name disruptive behaviour against the Boardroom Manipulation Tactics rather than describing it — The Assassin, cold logic used to shut down creative discussion, scorched-earth tactics.
Issue a Yellow Card to put a partner on notice, citing the agreed response time — from immediate or 24 hours through to 90 days — before any demerits are applied.
If the behaviour is not corrected in that window, apply the Conduct & Effect matrix to calculate the demerit points, combining a base score with the severity of the effect.
Track the running total: 20 points within 12 months triggers immediate resignation and trade restrictions.
Apply the bonus system in the same disciplined way — a partner generating more than $100k in new combined client fees earns the set bonus before profit share is calculated.

advisor_guidance.promotion_decisions_are_culture_signals: Every promotion decision in a professional services firm is read by the entire team as a signal of what the firm actually values — not what it says it values. A promotion of a technically excellent but relationship-poor partner sends the message that relationship skills are optional. Use the checklist consistently, and when candidates fall short of it, be explicit about why and what the development pathway is.
advisor_guidance.conduct_management_at_senior_level_requi: The most important conduct management interventions are at the most senior levels, where the cultural impact is greatest. The most common failure is allowing poor conduct at the partner level to persist because the managing partner is conflict-averse, or because the conduct is being tolerated in exchange for the individual's financial contribution. Financial contribution does not exempt any individual from the firm's conduct standards.
advisor_guidance.enneagram_is_a_tool_not_a_label: The Enneagram's value in leadership contexts is creating self-awareness and mutual understanding — not providing a categorisation that excuses behaviour. A Type 8 partner who is consistently aggressive cannot attribute their behaviour to their type. The type provides the language for understanding the motivation; the leader is still responsible for managing the behaviour. Use the profiling to open conversations, not to close them.
advisor_guidance.ethics_systems_only_work_if_applied_cons: A demerit system that is applied rigorously to junior partners and inconsistently to senior partners is worse than no system at all — it creates resentment and signals that the firm's ethics standards are performative. Before implementing the demerit system, the managing partner must be genuinely prepared to apply it at all levels of the partnership, including to themselves.
